newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Space Agency names Satellite inquiry board. [CORRECTED 15:30 GMT]
newsitem.headline: French Space Agency names Satellite inquiry board. [CORRECTED 15:30 GMT]

text.p: The French Space Agency CNES said on Wednesday it had named an inquiry board to investigate the failure of the SPOT-3 earth observation satellite which stopped functioning on November 14 after three years in orbit.
The eight-member board, led by Joel Barre of France's Defence Procurement Agency (DGA), is to report its findings by the end of this month.
CNES blamed SPOT-3's failure on a loss of attitude control. Attempts to reestablish contact with the satellite have failed.

The Spot Image Company, which markets SPOT satellite data, said an earlier generation satellite, SPOT-2, remained operational. It said efforts would now be made to reactivate the initial SPOT-1 satellite to avoid disruption of its services.
The SPOT satellites circle the earth at an altitude of 822 km (510 miles).
(Corrects the final paragraph by removing incorrect information about the satellites orbit, allowing it to remain stationary relative to the earth's surface.)
